'''Gagandeep Kang''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]<ref name=frs/> (born 3 November 1962) is an Indian public healthresearcher who has been leading the work on enteric diseases, diagnostics, genomics and epidemiology  at the [[Gates Foundation]] since 2023.<ref>E Kumar Sharma (15 November 2022), [https://www.financialexpress.com/healthcare/indias-ace-virologist-dr-gagandeep-kang-to-join-gates-foundation-as-director-global-health/2815918/ India's ace virologist Dr Gagandeep Kang to join Gates foundation as director, global health] ''[[The Financial Express (India)|The Financial Express]]''.</ref>

Kang was on the faculty of the Christian Medical College, [[Vellore]] from 1991 to 2023 when she retired as a Senior Professor in the Department of Gastrointestinal Sciences at the Christian Medical College, [[Vellore]], India.<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref> From August 2016 to August 2020, she was the Executive Director of the [[Translational Health Science and Technology Institute]], Faridabad, an autonomous institute of the Department of Biotechnology, Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=http://www.infosys-science-foundation.com/prize/laureates/2016/gagandeep-kang.asp|title=Infosys Prize – Laureates 2016 – Prof. Gagandeep Kang|website=Infosys-science-foundation.com|language=en|access-date=2018-01-20}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Gagandeep Kang : Hic Vac |url=https://www.hic-vac.org/members/members-profiles/professor-gagandeep-kang |website=www.hic-vac.org |access-date=25 November 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Raghavan |first1=Prabha |title=Gagandeep Kang, vaccine scientist, quits top research institute |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/india/gagandeep-kang-vaccine-scientist-quits-top-research-institute-6493337/ |website=The Indian Express |access-date=25 November 2020 |language=en |date=7 July 2020}}</ref> Her major research focus is on viral infections in children, and the testing of [[Rotavirus vaccine|rotaviral vaccines]]. She also works on other enteric infections and their consequences when children are infected in early life, sanitation and water safety. Her early research was on understanding the transmission and pathogenesis of infectious diseases, particularly those affecting children in developing countries. She was awarded the prestigious [[Infosys Prize]] in Life Sciences in 2016 for her contributions to understanding the natural history of rotavirus and other infectious diseases.<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://indiabioscience.org/columns/conversations/10-women-10-questions-gagandeep-kang|title=10 women, 10 questions: Gagandeep Kang|first=Harini|last=Barath|date=7 March 2017|website=IndiaBioscience.org|access-date=23 April 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.tropicalparasitology.org/article.asp?issn=2229-5070;year=2017;volume=7;issue=2;spage=128;epage=130;aulast=;type=0|title=An E-mail Interview with Prof. Gagandeep Kang|date=1 July 2017|journal=Tropical Parasitology|volume=7|issue=2|pages=128–130|access-date=23 April 2019|doi=10.4103/tp.TP_30_17|doi-broken-date=12 July 2025|doi-access=free|pmid=29114495|pmc=5652053}}</ref> In 2019, she became the first, and so far, the only, Indian woman to be elected as a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/science/gagandeep-kang-becomes-first-indian-woman-to-be-elected-royal-society-fellow/article26887069.ece|title=Gagandeep Kang becomes first Indian woman to be elected Royal Society Fellow|date=2019-04-19|work=The Hindu|access-date=2019-10-02|language=en-IN|issn=0971-751X}}</ref> In 2023, she was elected to the US National Academy of Medicine in recognition of her contributions to child health. She received the Canada John Dirks Gairdner Prize in Global Health in 2024 for the establishment of multiple birth cohort studies that resulted in a clearer understanding of differences in patterns of enteric infections in different parts of the world.

She has made significant contributions to policy development for vaccination and for public health, working with the Government of India and the World Health Organization by serving on advisory committees.

Kang co-authored the 2020 book ''[[Till We Win: India's Fight Against The COVID-19 pandemic]]'', with [[Chandrakant Lahariya]], a  [[public policy]] and [[health system]] expert and [[Randeep Guleria]], then director of [[AIIMS]], [[New Delhi]]. The book was published by publisher [[Penguin Random House]] in India.

==Early life and education==
Gagandeep Kang was born in [[Shimla]] on 3 November 1962.<ref name="ramesh">{{cite web |last1=Ramesh |first1=Sandhya |title=Meet Gagandeep Kang, Shimla scientist who's helping save lives of thousands of Indian kids |url=https://theprint.in/science/how-a-shimla-woman-is-helping-save-lives-of-thousands-of-kids-in-india-every-year/225439/ |website=ThePrint |access-date=25 November 2020 |date=24 April 2019}}</ref> Her mother taught English and history and her father was a [[mechanical engineering|mechanical engineer]] in the [[Indian Railways]].<ref name="ramesh"/> Kang grew up moving around north and east India, changing schools frequently. To catch up with curricula in each school, her father and she built a lab to conduct experiments in physics and chemistry.<ref name="Mohan">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/blink/meet/stick-it-out-and-make-good-friends-says-gagandeep-kang/article26952625.ece|title='Stick it out and make good friends'|last=Mohan|first=Shriya|website=@businessline|date=26 April 2019 |language=en|access-date=2019-10-02}}</ref>

Kang completed her [[Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery]] (MBBS) in 1987 and her [[Doctor of Medicine]] (MD) in Microbiology in 1991 from [[Christian Medical College, Vellore]] and obtained her [[PhD]] in 1998.<ref name="auto" /> She obtained her membership of the [[Royal College of Pathologists]] in 2000 and carried out [[postdoctoral research]] with [[Mary K. Estes]] at the [[Baylor College of Medicine|Baylor College of Medicine, Houston]] before returning to the Christian Medical College.

== Career and research ==
Kang is a medical scientist who has worked on diarrhea diseases and public health in India since the early 1990s. She is a key contributor to [[Rotavirus]] epidemiology and vaccinology in [[India]]. Focusing on vaccines, enteric infections and nutrition in young children in disadvantaged communities, she has combined field epidemiology with intensive laboratory investigations to inform both the science of infectious diseases and policy in India. Her comprehensive research on rotavirus has demonstrated the high burden of rotavirus disease across India, the genetic diversity of viruses, the lower protection from infection and vaccines and the exploration of several approaches to improve the performance of oral vaccines. Her work has led to her being described as India's "vaccine godmother".<ref name="Mohan"/>

Kang has published over 450 scientific papers and is or was on editorial boards for several journals. She was on many review committees for national and international research funding agencies, and has served on several advisory committees mainly related to vaccines, including India's [[National Immunization Technical Advisory Group|National Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation]], the WHO's [[Global Advisory Committee on Vaccine Safety]] and the Immunisation and Vaccine Implementation Research Advisory Committee. She chairs the WHO SEAR's Regional Immunisation Technical Advisory Group (2015–present). She has received honorary appointments as an associate faculty member at the [[Johns Hopkins University]] Bloomberg School of Public Health in Baltimore, Maryland and adjunct professor at [[Tufts University School of Medicine]] in Boston, Massachusetts.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://rotacouncil.org/about/council-members/gagandeep-kang/|title=Gagandeep Kang|website=Rota Council|language=en-US|access-date=2019-10-02}}</ref> She is a Fellow of the Royal College of Pathologists, the UK Faculty of Public Health, the American Academy of Microbiology and of Indian Academy of Sciences, National Academy of Sciences in India and the Indian National Science Academy, as well as the Royal Society.

Kang played a significant role in the efforts that culminated in the development of [[Rotavirus vaccine|Rotavac]], a vaccine from [[Bharat Biotech]] that targets [[diarrhea]]. She was one of three [[principal investigator]]s in the Phase III [[clinical trial]]s of the vaccine.<ref name=bbi>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bharatbiotech.com/images/press/Bharat_Biotech_2013_press_english.pdf|title=Rotavirus Vaccine Developed in India Demonstrates Strong Efficacy|date=2013-05-14|website=BharatBiotech.com|access-date=2019-04-28}}</ref> Her initial interest was in identifying the [[Correlates of immunity/correlates of protection|correlates of protection]] against the rotavirus. She and others began by recreating a study conducted in Mexico to identify children protected from rotaviral infection, research the [[immune response]]s and isolate the correlate of protection. The recreated study itself did not succeed, but it did develop high quality laboratory methods for the detection of rotaviruses. Kang and one of her students subsequently established [[Vaccine efficacy|vaccine assays]] for rotavirus infections, used in testing Rotavac.<ref name=interview>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/science/my-best-collaborators-are-women-says-gagandeep-kang-the-first-indian-woman-fellow-of-the-royal-society/article26952386.ece|title=My best collaborators are women, says Gagandeep Kang|date=2019-04-26|website=TheHindu.com|access-date=2019-04-28}}</ref>

During the COVID-19 pandemic, Kang played an influential role in science communication by writing op-eds, speaking online and in interviews on television, and serving as a credible voice against misinformation. She was part of the COVID-19 vaccine safety working group at WHO and the COVID-19 vaccine working group of the National Technical Advisory Group on Immunization.

* Global Health Centre, [[Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies]], Member of the International Advisory Board (2020-2023)<ref>[https://www.graduateinstitute.ch/GHC-IAB Global Health Centre International Advisory Board] [[Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies]], press release of April 20, 2020.</ref>
* [[Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations]] (CEPI), Member of the Board (2018–2023)<ref>Hannah Kuchler (19 January 2022), [https://www.ft.com/content/c1ab6cee-4f84-4a85-9c53-9f5f444359d4 Bill Gates warns of pandemics potentially far worse than Covid] ''[[Financial Times]]''.</ref><ref>[https://cepi.net/news_cepi/cepi-board-membership-updates-2/ CEPI Board membership updates] [[Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations]] (CEPI), press release of 5 April 2023.</ref>
* [[Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation]], Member of the Global Health Scientific Advisory Committee<ref>[https://www.gatesfoundation.org/about/leadership/scientific-advisory-committee Global Health Scientific Advisory Committee (2018-2023)] [[Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation]].</ref>

==Recognition==
Kang is the first Indian woman scientist to be elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]] (FRS) in 359 years of history of this scientific academy.<ref name=indytimes/> She was the ninth woman and the first physician-scientist to be awarded an Infosys Prize. She is the first Indian and the first woman to edit Manson's Textbook of Tropical Medicine.<ref name="auto"/> Other awards and honours include:

* 1998–1999 – Dr. P.N. Berry Fellowship<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://thsti.res.in/profile/Gagandeep-Kang|title=Translational Health Science and Technology Institute|website=thsti.res.in|access-date=2019-07-02}}</ref>
* 2005 – The Lourdu Yedanapalli Award for Excellence in Research<ref name=":0" />
* 2006 – Woman Bioscientist of the Yearś<ref name=":0" />
* 2016 – [[Infosys Prize]] in Life Sciences<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.livemint.com/Companies/SvjjeJV9APCdhQzx3HvD3M/Winners-of-Infosys-Prize-2016-announced.html|title=Winners of Infosys Prize 2016 announced|date=2016-11-18|website=Livemint.com/|access-date=2017-04-03}}</ref>
* 2019 – Elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS)<ref name="frs">{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/gagandeep-kang-14102/|title=Gagandeep Kang – Royal Society|website=Royalsociety.org|access-date=23 April 2019}}</ref><ref name="indytimes">{{cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/gagandeep-kang-enters-royal-society-of-london-as-first-indian-woman-scientist-fellow/articleshow/68944435.cms|title=Gagandeep Kang enters Royal Society of London as first Indian woman scientist fellow – Times of India|newspaper=[[The Times of India]]|access-date=23 April 2019}}</ref>
* 2024 – [[Canada Gairdner Global Health Award]]<ref>[https://www.gairdner.org/winners Canada Gairdner Global Health Award 2024]</ref>
